axis: liable to a penalty → condemned for grave wrong

members.tone: The family's plain verdict, covering both the one who did the reprehensible act and the one merely chargeable with it - responsibility and accusation under a single word.
Mildest of the blame words, locating blame without characterising the deed, where *guilty* already calls the act reprehensible.
Weighs the deed and finds it has earned censure, a considered verdict rather than *at fault*'s bare attribution.
Flat and formal, stating only that blame may properly be laid, without *blameworthy*'s sense that the deed went out and earned it.
Equally impersonal, taking the wrong, the evil and the merely injurious alike without changing temperature.
Puts the blame inside the thing as a quality it is full of, where *blameworthy* says only that blame is deserved.
Pitches the fault toward reproof that could be pronounced out loud, the most public-facing of these.
The coolest of these, recording fault as a determination, which is why it sits as easily on the injurious as on the evil.
The gravest here - guilt of killing rather than of a misdeed, and the word treats it as a stain carried rather than a charge answered.
Neutral and procedural, recording exposure to accusation and resting as readily on the cause as on the person, so it asserts no wrong.
Weights that same liability toward formal accusation, sounding graver than *chargeable* while claiming no more guilt.
The one inward member, guilt felt from inside rather than laid on from outside, with the conscience itself doing the striking.
Hard and total, making the wrongdoing a category the person belongs to, and it reaches past crime proper to any serious offense.
Lighter than *criminal* by the size of the deed, chiding a misdeed rather than condemning a crime.
Purely procedural, measuring the offence as money owed and judging the offender not at all.
As bloodless as *finable* - a penalty attaches, and nothing is said about the wrong or the wrongdoer.
